text: What is the capital of Morocco?
explanation: Rabat is the administrative and political capital of the Kingdom of Morocco.

text: How many days are there in a week?
explanation: A week has seven days.

text: Which animal is known as the king of the jungle?
explanation: The lion earned the title for its strength and presence, even though it mostly lives on the savannah.

text: How many colours are there in a rainbow?
explanation: Its seven colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

text: Which planet do we live on?
explanation: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only one known to support life.

text: In which month do Muslims fast?
explanation: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Hijri calendar, and fasting in it is one of the pillars of Islam.

text: What do bees mainly make honey from?
explanation: Bees collect nectar from flowers and turn it into honey inside the hive.

text: How many players does a football team have on the pitch?
explanation: Each team plays with eleven players, including the goalkeeper.

text: What is the largest ocean in the world?
explanation: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about a third of the Earth's surface.

text: On which continent is most of Egypt located?
explanation: Most of Egypt is in north-east Africa; the Sinai Peninsula is in Asia.

text: Which gas do we need to breathe to stay alive?
explanation: The body's cells need oxygen to produce energy.

text: How many legs does a spider have?
explanation: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs, while insects have six.

text: What is the official currency of Saudi Arabia?
explanation: The Saudi riyal is the kingdom's official currency.

text: Which season comes after winter?
explanation: The seasons go winter, spring, summer, autumn.

text: What is 9 × 9?
explanation: Nine times nine is eighty-one.

text: What is the longest river in Africa?
explanation: At about 6,650 km, the Nile is Africa's longest river.

text: Which animal is known as the ship of the desert?
explanation: The camel copes with thirst and heat and can cover long distances across the desert.

text: How many letters are there in the Arabic alphabet?
explanation: The Arabic alphabet has twenty-eight letters, from alif to ya.

text: What is the capital of France?
explanation: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, and home to the Eiffel Tower.

text: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
explanation: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body through the blood vessels.

text: Who wrote the "Muqaddimah"?
explanation: Ibn Khaldun wrote it in the 14th century and is regarded as a pioneer of sociology.

text: What is the smallest planet in the Solar System?
explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun (Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006).

text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
explanation: Au comes from the Latin aurum; Ag is the symbol for silver.

text: In which year was the first FIFA World Cup held?
explanation: The first tournament was played in 1930 in Uruguay, which also won it.

text: What is the highest mountain in the world above sea level?
explanation: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas, rises to about 8,849 metres.

text: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
explanation: An adult skeleton has 206 bones; babies are born with more, some of which fuse as they grow.

text: What is the capital of Canada?
explanation: Ottawa is Canada's capital, although Toronto is its largest city.

text: Who painted the "Mona Lisa"?
explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted it in the early 16th century; it hangs in the Louvre.

text: What is the largest Arab country by area?
explanation: Algeria is the largest country in both the Arab world and Africa, at about 2.38 million km².

text: What is the fastest land animal?
explanation: The cheetah can reach nearly 110 km/h over short distances.

text: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air, oxygen about 21%.

text: In which city is the University of al-Qarawiyyin?
explanation: Founded in Fez by Fatima al-Fihri in 859, it is one of the oldest universities in the world.

text: How many surahs are there in the Quran?
explanation: The Quran has 114 surahs, from Al-Fatiha to An-Nas.

text: Which language does Google recommend first for building Android apps?
explanation: In 2019 Google announced that Android development would be "Kotlin-first".

text: What is the largest planet in the Solar System?
explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

text: Who developed the theory of relativity?
explanation: Einstein published special relativity in 1905 and general relativity in 1915.

text: What is the capital of Australia?
explanation: Canberra was chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

text: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C under normal atmospheric pressure.

text: Which strait separates Morocco from Spain?
explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar links the Mediterranean to the Atlantic and is about 14 km wide at its narrowest.

text: Which is the only mammal capable of true flight?
explanation: Bats are the only mammals that truly fly; flying squirrels only glide.

text: In which year did Tariq ibn Ziyad cross into al-Andalus?
explanation: Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed in 711 the strait that now bears his name: Gibraltar comes from "Jabal Tariq".

text: What is the deepest known point in the oceans?
explanation: The Challenger Deep, in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific, is almost 11 km deep.

text: Who wrote "The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing" (al-jabr)?
explanation: Al-Khwarizmi laid the foundations of algebra, and the word "algorithm" comes from his name.

text: What is the atomic number of carbon?
explanation: A carbon nucleus has 6 protons; 12 is the mass number of its most common isotope.

text: Who wrote the "Book of Optics" (Kitab al-Manazir), which revolutionised optics?
explanation: Ibn al-Haytham showed through experiments that we see because light travels from objects into the eye.

text: Roughly how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
explanation: Light travels at about 299,792 km per second.

text: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
explanation: Mandarin has the most native speakers; English has the most speakers overall.

text: In which year did Granada, the last Muslim stronghold in al-Andalus, fall?
explanation: Boabdil surrendered Granada in 1492, the same year Christopher Columbus reached the Americas.

text: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
explanation: The Sahara is the largest hot desert; the largest desert of all is Antarctica.

text: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
explanation: Vatican City covers about 0.44 km² in the heart of Rome.

text: Who founded the Idrisid dynasty in Morocco?
explanation: Idris ibn Abdallah founded the Idrisid dynasty in 788, the first independent Muslim state in Morocco.

text: How many chromosomes are there in a human body cell?
explanation: A body (somatic) cell has 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs; a sex cell has 23.

text: Which planet takes the longest to spin once on its axis?
explanation: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once, longer than its year of 225 days.

text: In which city was the United Nations Charter signed in 1945?
explanation: The Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945 and came into force that October.

text: Which gas makes up most of the atmosphere of Mars?
explanation: Mars has a very thin atmosphere made of about 95% carbon dioxide.

text: Who wrote "Nuzhat al-Mushtaq" and drew its famous map of the world?
explanation: Al-Idrisi completed the work in 1154 for King Roger II of Sicily.

text: Which Moroccan traveller wrote the "Rihla" (Tuhfat al-Nuzzar)?
explanation: Born in Tangier in 1304, Ibn Battuta travelled the Muslim world and beyond for nearly thirty years.

text: What is the unit of electric current?
explanation: The ampere measures current, the volt voltage, the ohm resistance and the watt power.

text: In which year did a human first walk on the Moon?
explanation: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969, and Neil Armstrong was the first to walk on it.

text: What is the longest bone in the human body?
explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the body.
